hints: Start by picturing the structure of propan-2-ol, notice the OH is on the middle carbon so it is a secondary alcohol.
Recall what each reagent type does to a secondary alcohol, oxidation to a ketone, dehydration to an alkene, or esterification.
Check the carbon skeleton in each product to see if it still matches a branched 3-carbon chain from propan-2-ol.
walkthrough:
**Draw propan-2-ol in your mind**

Propan-2-ol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. The OH is on carbon 2.

That makes it a secondary alcohol, so its chemistry is fixed and predictable.

**Recall the four key reaction types**

Oxidation with acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ turns a secondary alcohol into a ketone:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$$
Conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ with heat dehydrates an alcohol to an alkene by removing $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Carboxylic acids esterify alcohols to give esters with the branched skeleton kept.

**Test each row against the rules**

Row with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This is propene, written as $\text{CH}_3\text{CHCH}_2$. The skeleton and reaction type both match perfectly, so this row is correct.

options.A: Incorrect. Acidified KMnO4 oxidises the secondary alcohol propan-2-ol to the ketone propanone, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$. The product shown, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$, is propanal, an aldehyde which can only come from oxidation of the primary alcohol propan-1-ol.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{Cl}_2$ alone does not replace the OH group by Cl. To make 2-chloropropane, $\text{CH}_3\text{CHClCH}_3$, you need $\text{HCl}$, $\text{PCl}_5$, $\text{PCl}_3$ or $\text{SOCl}_2$. This is a common trap confusing alkane free-radical chlorination with alcohol substitution.
options.C: Correct. Concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ dehydrates propan-2-ol by elimination of water to form propene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2$, shown as $\text{CH}_3\text{CHCH}_2$. This is the standard dehydration of a secondary alcohol.
options.D: Incorrect. Methanoic acid, $\text{HCOOH}$, does esterify with propan-2-ol, but the alkyl group must stay branched as $\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$. The correct ester is isopropyl methanoate, $\text{HCO}_2\text{CH(CH}_3)_2$. The product shown, $\text{HCO}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is the n-propyl ester from propan-1-ol.
